summary: Point the credential metadata at BOOKCLICKER_SESSION, the env var the spec declares: auth_env_vars in .printing-press.json, and the MCP server env plus user_config in manifest.json.
reason: generate emits PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE as this CLI's credential on some runs even though the spec's auth block declares env_vars: [BOOKCLICKER_SESSION]. That name is the framework's tenant-gated client-profile selector, not this CLI's credential; this CLI authenticates with a Rails session cookie and configures no client-profile source. In manifest.json the effect is functional, not cosmetic: server.mcp_config.env mapped PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, so an MCP host would prompt for a "Client profile" and the server would never receive the session cookie, failing auth on every tool call. The user_config entry also lacked sensitive: true, unlike every other credential-bearing CLI in this category. The value flapped across reprints and a reprint with BOOKCLICKER_SESSION exported still produced the wrong one, so it follows neither the spec nor the environment. The library's Validate MCPB manifest contract check caught the manifest half.
validated_outcome: publish validate passes 11/11; the MCPB manifest contract check requires server.mcp_config.env to contain the declared auth env vars, and now does. The env/user_config shape matches sibling CLIs (erank, everbee, dub, beehiiv). Re-check both files after any regen or lock promote, which regenerate them and revert this.
